chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: Segregated hotels on tour and the Goodman films
summary: Wilson and Hampton stayed in Negro hotels rather than fight each town, and the band films first excluded and then carefully separated the quartet.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, how about in your tours, did you have any problem hotel-wise or restaurant-wise?

Yes, but that was -- it's hard to call that a problem because it was the norm of that day. We didn't challenge the norm, which was that Lionel and I couldn't stay in the white hotels. If we'd had to make a battle of that thing in every town on one-night stands; you couldn't ever get to work, making an issue of that. So Lionel and I generally would drive our cars and go into the Negro district of town

and go to a Negro hotel, see. And we'd just go and do the job. We were not going to fight the whole city hall thing that way, make an issue of it. We went along with the tide the way it was, because we had opened up a door already, a giant crack, and there was no need of making a big fuss. Because the door gradually opened of its own accord, opened wide as we have today. But that was the first cracking of the door. And I think it was correct to do it that way and not -- but this is the first move.

I think earlier on the tape we mentioned that the first movie of the Goodman Band I wasn't in because they were afraid to photograph me. They wanted me to do the soundtrack but they didn't want to photograph me playing the piano.
That was a movie called "Big Broadcast" of 1937 -- '36.

But the next year it was the "Hollywood Hotel" movie, the next movie the band was in. I was photographed and so was Lionel Hampton. Lionel had joined us by then, and we were both photographed. But in a segment that didn't interfere with the story so any prejudiced distributors could cut the quartet scene out if they wanted. The story, the Hollywood Hotel story would proceed. But they had a very nice segment of us playing a few numbers with the quartet,

So we took every situation as we came to it and we didn't fight to overcome the racial restrictions of the hotels and the restaurants where we knew we'd have a battle. In some areas, of course, our road manager could have sounded out a lot of situations out in advance and know what we were walking into before us, you know, checking with hotels, whether the entire group would be welcome or not. So we knew a lot of that.
